findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the primary-verifier cache description: the message-tail arm applies an automatic tail breakpoint (anthropic_cache/bedrock_cache_messages), not a positional 'CachePoint after the fence'; state the benefit as reduced opening round-trips over the byte-stable leading context.

runner.py:664-666 documents Anthropic sends a TOP-LEVEL cache_control at the end of the prompt

findings.finding: The primary-verifier caching mechanism is misdescribed: it claims a 'CachePoint after the fenced block' on the message-tail arm, but that arm (anthropic_cache / bedrock_cache_messages) applies an automatic whole-tail breakpoint with no per-block CachePoint API, and Anthropic emits a top-level cache_control.
scenarios: Implementer tries to insert an explicit CachePoint after the fence and finds the message-tail arm exposes no such control, then wastes effort or adds an unsupported mechanism
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: the prefetch sits in the byte-stable leading part of the fenced context so it is cache-read under the existing message-tail arm; there is no separate per-block CachePoint to add.

findings.finding: operations.assemble_context is a SHARED context-builder also consumed by the general review op (operations.py:195 review_ticket) and its workflow wrapper (review_workflows.py:53), not only the completion gate; keying the prefetch purely off assemble_context's existing `graph` flag would inject prefetched file contents into the general-review path on any graph=True call, where the completion_verifier.md trust/anti-anchoring paragraph does NOT apply.
findings.location: Scope: 'src/rebar/llm/operations.py — assemble_context seam for prefetched file contents + commit diffs, keyed off its existing graph flag'
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit opt-in argument to assemble_context (e.g. `prefetch: PrefetchSpec | None = None`) set only by gate_ops.py for the completion gate; leave review_ticket / review_workflows callers passing prefetch=None so their output stays byte-identical, and note this in Scope + an AC.

findings.finding: The subject plan rides the message-tail caching arm and places a hand-authored CachePoint after the fenced block (capabilities.py:684-696) for the primary verifier prefetch. The prerequisite explicitly rejects a hand-placed CachePoint, stating the shared cache is the EXISTING automatic prompt-cache and that the message-tail arm places the breakpoint at the message-tail END, the provider-managed prefix cache, NOT a hand-placed CachePoint after the ticket block. These two plans make conflicting design decisions about how the same message-tail cache arm is used in the same agentic completion verifier.

evidence: Subject: 'Recovery builds an INDEPENDENT RunRequest per criterion (completion_recovery.py:580-598 constructs a fresh RunRequest(system_prompt=_EVIDENCE_SYSTEM, instructions=...) inside the per-criterion loop)'

Subject: 'it is realized as a BYTE-STABLE prefetch block placed at a FIXED position in the recovery system_prompt via cache_prefix ... CACHE-READ on every criterion after the first ... cache-read across the N independent per-criterion runs'
Prerequisite: 'Replace the per-criterion fan-out (completion_recovery.py _recover, deleted not dead-coded) with banked incremental verification'
Prerequisite: 'Runs = ceil(remainder/cap), sequential, each ONE batched agentic run — never per-criterion'
Prerequisite AC: 'The per-criterion fan-out is removed: no code path in completion_recovery.py launches one LLM run per criterion'
findings.finding: The subject plan's recovery-successor prefetch design is explicitly predicated on the per-criterion fan-out that this prerequisite deletes and replaces with batched successor runs. The subject states recovery 'builds an INDEPENDENT RunRequest per criterion (completion_recovery.py:580-598 constructs a fresh RunRequest ... inside the per-criterion loop); those N runs share no message history' and derives its cache economy as being 'CACHE-READ on every criterion after the first ... across the N per-criterion runs'. The prerequisite removes exactly this loop ('Replace the per-criterion fan-out (completion_recovery.py _recover, deleted not dead-coded) with banked incremental verification', 'no code path in completion_recovery.py launches one LLM run per criterion') in favor of batched successor runs (ceil(remainder/cap), '<=8 criteria/batch', 'never per-criterion'). After the prerequisite ships there are no 'N per-criterion runs' for the subject's byte-stable cache_prefix block to be cache-read across; the subject's cited line anchors and its per-criterion cache-economy premise no longer hold.
scenarios: Prerequisite lands first: recovery is batched, so the subject's 'byte-stable block cache-read across the N per-criterion runs' and its line references (580-598, per-criterion loop) are stale; the subject's acceptance criterion pinning 'byte-stable block at a fixed system_prompt position ... cache-read across the N independent per-criterion runs' cannot be satisfied as written.
findings.suggested_fix: Rework the subject's recovery-successor prefetch to attach the byte-stable cache_prefix block to the batched successor runs (ceil(remainder/cap)) introduced by this prerequisite, and update the per-criterion line/loop references and acceptance criterion accordingly.

findings.finding: The plan asserts the prefetch section rides the message-tail caching arm 'with a CachePoint after the fenced block,' but the cited arm (capabilities.py:684-701) uses pydantic-ai's automatic-caching keys where the breakpoint placement is not caller-controlled: for Anthropic 'anthropic_cache=True ... sends a TOP-LEVEL cache_control so the server places the breakpoint at the END of the prompt' and Bedrock 'REJECTS a top-level cache_control outright.' No seam in the codebase places an explicit CachePoint after an arbitrary message position, so the plan depends on a caching capability the integration as-used does not provide.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that the prefetch rides at the byte-stable HEAD of the message tail so the automatic end-of-tail breakpoint (anthropic_cache/bedrock_cache_messages) still covers it, and remove the 'CachePoint after the fenced block' language which implies caller-controlled placement the seam does not offer; if a specific breakpoint position is truly required, route it to a SPIKE against pydantic-ai's message-caching API.
